headline: At each endpoint, track both the best increasing length and how many ways attain it
statement: Count index-distinct longest strictly increasing subsequences of nums. A subsequence may skip elements but preserves their original index order.
constraints: The answer fits a signed 32-bit integer
intuition: At each endpoint, track both the best increasing length and how many ways attain it. Equal-valued elements are separate choices but cannot extend each other.
approach: Initialize length[i]=1 and ways[i]=1 for every endpoint.
For each earlier j with nums[j]<nums[i], consider length[j]+1.
Replace ways[i] when this improves the length; add ways[j] when it ties.
Sum ways at endpoints whose length equals the global maximum.
correctness: Every non-singleton increasing subsequence ending at i has a unique previous index j with smaller value. The transition selects the largest achievable length and sums disjoint counts classified by that j. Induction over i establishes each length/count pair; summing optimal endpoints counts each global longest subsequence once.
bruteForce: Enumerate all 2^n index subsets and test whether their values increase.

complexity.explanation: Time O(n²); auxiliary space O(n). Output storage is excluded unless stated.

pitfalls: Strict comparison excludes equal adjacent values.
Reset the count on an improved length; add only on an equal best length.
Sum counts across all longest endpoints, not just the last one.
